integration_issues.flow: FEATURE 3c — APK auto-login redeem on app boot via ?ah=TOKEN
integration_issues.issue: Navigating to https://<host>/?ah=<token> does NOT auto-login the user. The /api/auth/redeem-apk-handoff endpoint is NEVER called by the SPA (verified via network capture). Root cause: /app/frontend/src/App.js line 237 — `<Route path="/" element={<Navigate to="/signup" replace />} />` performs a synchronous client-side redirect that drops the query string before AuthProvider's useEffect runs. By the time AuthContext.redeemHandoff() reads window.location.search, the ?ah= param has already been wiped, so params.get('ah') is null and the call returns false. User ends up at /signup (not /dashboard), with no matka11_token in localStorage.

action_items: FIX FEATURE 3c: AuthContext.redeemHandoff() runs too late because App.js synchronously redirects from '/' to '/signup' via <Navigate replace> which drops the query string. Options: (a) capture window.location.search into a module-level variable in AuthContext.js at module load time (before React mounts) and read from that variable inside redeemHandoff; (b) change the '/' route in App.js to render a small <HandoffGate /> component that defers redirection until AuthProvider has finished its boot (or that itself reads ?ah= and calls redeem); (c) make Navigate preserve query: <Navigate to={'/signup' + window.location.search} replace />, AND also do the same on any other catch-all redirect that runs before AuthProvider mounts. Recommended: option (a) — add `const BOOT_AH = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('ah');` at top of AuthContext.js and have redeemHandoff use BOOT_AH instead of re-reading window.location.search.

After fix, also ensure the user lands on /dashboard after successful redeem (currently AuthContext sets user but the route may still resolve to /signup if redirect already happened). Use navigate('/dashboard', {replace:true}) inside the redeem-success branch, or rely on the user-based PrivateRoute re-evaluation.
critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.js redeemHandoff reads window.location.search inside useEffect — this is unreliable because React Router's top-level Navigate at '/' runs synchronously during the first render and strips the query string before useEffect fires. Capture ?ah at module-load time.

Backend _apk_handoff_store is process-memory. Acceptable for 10-min TTL as noted, but document that a backend restart between create+redeem invalidates tokens. Consider moving to Redis or MongoDB collection with TTL index for production.

TelegramWelcomePopup.js handleDownload() ignores axios errors silently (console.warn only). User won't see any visible cue if handoff creation fails — consider showing a toast/inline message so the user understands no auto-login link will appear.
Pre-existing React warning still present: 'A props object containing a "key" prop is being spread into JSX' for <Link> elements — unchanged from iter 22, not blocking but should be cleaned up.

rca of the issue: Race condition between React Router's synchronous Navigate at route '/' (App.js:237) and AuthProvider's asynchronous redeemHandoff inside useEffect. Reproduction: open fresh incognito → goto /?ah=<valid_token> → router immediately swaps URL to /signup (replace) which discards the ?ah= query string → AuthProvider.useEffect runs redeemHandoff → window.location.search === '' → params.get('ah') === null → redeemHandoff returns false without ever calling /api/auth/redeem-apk-handoff → checkAuth() runs → /api/auth/me 401 → user remains anonymous on /signup. Mitigation: read ?ah= at module-import time in AuthContext (before any React render / router redirect) and pass the captured value into redeemHandoff.
